approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. Ordinary proposals come from a source-conditioned graph editor that adds corpus-derived attachment fragments or deletes directed bridge sides; crossover and bounded ordinary fallback remain available. A count-fingerprint Gaussian process selects purchases from the generated field, and accepted scores update the archive and breeding population. The editor learns from every purchased represented action, using a positive, frozen exponential weight relative to the incumbent at announcement. Its sampler conditions the joint add/delete law on construction failures and already-seen products, but replay currently fits the unconditioned action likelihood.
approach.novelty: Fit each replay action under the admission-conditioned distribution that existed immediately before its proposal. Save that historical support and differentiate its complete joint normalizer at the current parameters. This changes one likelihood and its gradient while keeping the Parent's weights, replay membership and sampler fixed. There are no supplied same-Parent siblings. Earlier editor children changed outcome caching, a hard success gate, or all-outcome weighting; none trained the historical masked likelihood. The test asks whether this distribution alignment increases total realized progress across ordinary and crossover purchases.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior on actual code Parent n-d781e302f9f5 is a directly implemented mismatch between the action law sampled by condition_distribution and the law fitted by action_log_prob, not missing replay or inactive learning. The complete Search panel has macro mean 0.5403905255824667, population SD 0.01643029222537268 and seed macros 0.534599748783005 / 0.562773908541947 / 0.523797919422448. Its paired code-Parent delta is -0.005614905141346993. All 2250 represented paid actions entered weighted replay (2077 negative, 26 tied, 147 positive); 10875 finite updates and 2166 later paid probability changes were recorded. Ordinary incumbent mass increased to 0.1668219340933813, but crossover mass decreased to 0.16507648044677622; their full-panel total is the frozen 0.3318984145401575. Mean paid raw/conditioned probabilities are 0.0686665142535886 / 0.09501657310406558, while training omits log_Z and its derivative. This establishes the mismatch, not that it caused the endpoint loss. Preserve n-d781e302f9f5 confirmed/not_triggered, n-db9d21d15567 incumbent-only replay refuted/triggered, and the earlier n-a8f828a5ff9b cache and n-cd97f70a82cb editor confirmations. Direct raw reconstruction is in policy/scratch/r0079-02-improve-L01/plan/parent-evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit-seed files, each citing its original Search log, trajectory, summary and run.log. Source analyses and the frozen planning evidence preserve low-ESS sessions, weak-learning blocks, every adverse cell and the terminal never-sampled action.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen r79-support-and-deployed-policy-review, specifically its position3 adoptions, with their exact off-policy/historical-mask deviations. sources.finding: Sampling a masked distribution while differentiating raw likelihood differs from differentiating the normalized policy. Raw-gradient cases can have higher return; normalization does not guarantee improvement.

hypothesis: Modify m-cd97f70a82cb by replacing only weighted raw-action imitation with weighted likelihood of the exact proposal-time admission-conditioned joint action law. For record i, retain its original source/support S_i and the exclusion set M_i known before that action draw. At current parameters theta compute ell_raw_theta(i), and log_Z_theta(i)=logsumexp of ell_raw_theta(a) over every a in S_i minus M_i, including both supported modes and their inherited raw factor 0.5. Train ell_hist_theta(i)=ell_raw_theta(i)-log_Z_theta(i), differentiating both terms. The loss is -sum_i(w_i*ell_hist_theta(i))/sum_i(w_i), with the exact inherited immutable real-feedback weights. This directs the existing replay gradient toward the probability of observed actions among their historically admissible alternatives. Its observable path is correct historical-support use -> nonzero normalizer-gradient exposure -> changed later paid probabilities/choices -> possibly increased full all-route incumbent mass. It changes no label, proposal law, replay membership, temperature, schedule or host decision consumer.

finding_summary.headline: Historical likelihood learning activates, but total realized progress falls; two tasks fail at shutdown
finding_summary.insights: Aligning the replay likelihood with the historically sampled distribution changed learning and later purchases, but did not deliver the predicted total progress in this panel. This settles the registered likelihood-alignment prediction, while leaving the broader editor approach and the Parent’s earlier confirmation intact. Neither borrowed normalization nor weighted regression guarantees better return in this off-policy, one-step setting. Learning was uneven: whole-replay mean conditioned likelihood worsened in 135 of 435 blocks and raw likelihood in 138; minibatch effective sample size ranged from about 1.06 to 31.70. These observations do not identify a causal mediator. Molecular evidence also rules out a blanket diversity-collapse diagnosis: pooled typed/generic scaffold coverage rose from 1042/802 to 1185/902, yet one upper-score group occupied only five typed and four generic scaffolds. Attachment chemistry remained inconsistent, all assigned atom stereocentres were absent, and both severe truncation and repeated-core growth persisted. A proposal method that can make coherent scaffold/linker replacements while preserving connected context could address this measured search limitation; a likelihood-denominator correction alone does not supply those capabilities. Whether such a method helps, and whether complete official score evidence changes the performance conclusion, remains open. Shutdown failure is an additional technical limitation, not evidence that learning never ran.
finding_summary.results: The saved-mask learner ran through all 435 training blocks and 10,875 updates. Every update had a nonzero normalizer gradient, all 2,191 later paid actions changed conditioned probability, and 2,077 changed their passive same-uniform action choice. Nevertheless full all-route incumbent progress averaged 0.3258107570 per session versus the Parent’s 0.3318984145, triggering the registered useful-transfer falsifier. Ordinary progress was 0.1662010388 versus 0.1668219341; crossover progress was 0.1596097182 versus 0.1650764804. Late total progress fell from 0.0849958851 to 0.0687627048. All 4,350 optimizer purchases and their 4,200 next-fit joins are retained. The two complete official seeds averaged 0.5322378780, with paired Parent deltas -0.0039148721 and -0.0289830292. Two seed-2 tasks failed to exit after stop despite complete behavioral logs; their official endpoints and the seed-2 macro remain unavailable, so the full +0.002 endpoint target cannot be assessed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyls, ring amines and enlarged fused cores; no assigned stereochemistry and uneven attachment chemistry
molecular.overall_character: The accepted products are predominantly connected, ring-rich aromatic molecules: indole carboxamides, heteroaryl and fused dione systems, aryl sulfonamides, piperazines, pyrrolidines and piperidines, with alkyl, alkoxy and halogen decoration. Conventional medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with N-nitroso, N/O-halogen, peroxide-like O-O, aminal and repeated-core structures. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, while drug-likeness is moderate as a structural reading only; neither synthesis, stability, efficacy nor toxicity was measured here. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9575 to 0.9736 and aromatic-text rates 0.9506 to 0.9701, supporting rich ring/aromatic content. Across the 4350 accepted optimizer rows, RDKit 2023.09.6 gives a heavy-atom median of 31, range 1 to 112, median 4 rings and median 3 aromatic rings. There are 142 products with at most 6 heavy atoms and 514 with at least 50, versus 154 and 432 in the Parent. These diagnostic size cutoffs are not proposed rewards or filters. Typed/generic Murcko coverage is 1185/902 versus Parent 1042/802, counting the empty scaffold once; this is increased pooled coverage with substantial local family concentration, not global collapse. No product in either panel has an assigned atom stereocentre; unassigned graph-perceived centres occur in 1902 Child and 1861 Parent products. N-halogen, O-halogen and single O-O flags occur in 156, 87 and 61 Child products versus 371, 156 and 95 Parent products. The O-O definition here is any single O-O bond and must not be pooled with historical divalent-peroxide counts. Neutral N=O and N-nitroso flags occur in 243 and 67 Child products versus 9 and 8 Parent products. All these are overlapping graph flags. All 15 request-indexed Child trajectories and all 15 published code-Parent trajectories were read in full: each has 10 initial and 290 optimizer rows, so there are no missing chemistry paths or omitted objectives. Initial rows are retained in the audits but excluded from optimizer descriptor populations. The record coverage is not formal completion: seeds 0/1 passed; seed 2 has three successful tasks and deco_hop/drd2_docking failed with candidate did not exit after stop after 300 calls each. Its canonical execution receipt remains retryable with exit_code 2, its summary remains buggy with val_score null, and no missing final task metric is reconstructed from the trajectory. The exact frozen comparison has child_complete=false and paired_complete=false, with only seeds 0/1 formally matched; the Parent has seeds 0/1/2. Chemical comparisons below include the observed third-seed structures while retaining this limitation. The analyzed implementation is the sealed repaired APPLY1; initial failed smoke and CPU repair fixtures contribute no formal Search chemistry. The trajectory source labels distinguish initial from optimizer only, so no ordinary/crossover or mechanism attribution is made. Final sampled molecules are not treated as best-so-far molecules. Upper/lower deciles below are the 87 highest/lowest existing-score optimizer rows per task, pooled over the three seeds with deterministic tie handling, not independent replicates or controlled molecular-pair tests. Definitions, all 15 session audits, original Search paths and byte-identical in-run copies are recorded in policy/scratch/r0079-02-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json and policy/scratch/r0079-02-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-measurements.json. Only original request-authorized trajectories and the digest authorize quoted molecules.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly trimethyl/methoxy-substituted indole carboxanilides and related carbonyl-linked aromatic systems: optimizer heavy atoms median 25, range 1 to 43, with median 3 rings and 3 aromatic rings. The seed-0 evaluation-271 and seed-2 evaluation-283 leader is a 23-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring indole carboxamide whose amide nitrogen bears N=O. The seed-1 leader instead joins the indole to a pyridyl group through a consecutive-dicarbonyl amide. Ordinary aryl-carbonyl backbones look synthetically interpretable, but many final attachments are unusual: neutral N=O occurs in 242/870 products, N-nitroso in 67, and N-halogen in 36. All 99 formally charged Child products belong to this task; charge notation alone does not establish useful protonation-state coverage. Compared with the Parent, typed/generic scaffold coverage is narrower here, 78/51 versus 99/63, despite the Child having broader pooled coverage across all tasks.
liabilities: N-nitroso amide, N-chloro amide and peroxide-like attachments make route and stability assessment necessary; their presence is a structural concern, not a toxicity conclusion.
The small charged fragment and other extreme truncations have lost the aromatic carbonyl context associated with the higher observed scores.
missing_features: Alternative coherent aromatic core/linker families that retain the observed carbonyl and aromatic context are weakly represented among the upper-scoring products; most variation is decoration of the indole family.

A set of matched, conventionally attached polar alternatives to the N-nitroso/N-chloro substitutions is missing. Their benefit is untested; the visible scores do not identify a hidden required pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed 0.4491253474628456 N-nitroso carboxamide and the 0.4259670894318899 seed-1 dicarbonyl amide retain an indole plus a second aromatic group and a carbonyl-rich connector. The quoted charged nitrogen/oxygen fragment scores 0.0; the lower decile contains all 27 products of at most 6 heavy atoms. All 87 upper-decile products have three rings, three aromatic rings and the explicitly defined carboxamide SMARTS flag; 52 have neutral N=O, compared with 4/87 in the Parent upper decile. Thus this sampled gradient preserves an aromatic carbonyl context and tolerates substantial nitroso decoration. It does not show that nitrosation itself causes gain or supplies a missing target interaction. The seed-2 last proposal, an N-chloro amide with an O-CH2-N=O substituent, scores 0.4103264278932849, below its earlier observed best.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most seed-dependent chemical stream: median 45 heavy atoms, range 1 to 97, median 4 rings and 4 aromatic rings. Seed 0 reaches an amino-substituted heteroaryl assembly with nitriles and a dialkylamino group, 30 heavy atoms and three rings. Seed 1 produces a 44-heavy-atom, four-aromatic-ring sulfur-rich molecule with thioethers and a central carbon attached to nitrogen and two sulfur substituents. Seed 2 produces 57-heavy-atom repeated fused dione cores connected through N-N, with ten perceived rings, six aromatic rings and an appended aminal-containing chain. That last structure is observed chemistry from a failed-stop session, not a valid formal endpoint. The broad collection includes 332/870 products at least 50 heavy atoms versus Parent 243/870. Upper-decile heavy-atom/ring medians are 55/10 versus Parent 44/6; the Parent also generated large heteroaromatics and charged assemblies, so this is a change of occupied structures, not the first appearance of complex chemistry.
liabilities: The N-N-linked fused-core dimer and aminal-rich appendage, and the sulfur-rich central junction, require credible connection chemistry; valence validity is not a synthetic route.
Very large repeated assemblies coexist with tiny fragments. Twenty-two products have at most six heavy atoms, so occupied size diversity includes substantial loss of connected molecular context.
missing_features: The record lacks systematic, coherent core/linker alternatives that preserve favorable connected context while avoiding repeated-core duplication or dense heteroatom junctions; the high-scoring compact examples show that large duplication is not the only observed route.

Configuration is not specified for the stereogenic sulfur-rich side-chain products: 374/870 products have unassigned graph-perceived centres and none has an assigned atom centre. No specific target-required group can be deduced from the broad, shallow observed score differences.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino/nitrile heteroaryl seed-0 molecule scores 0.6039881972206358, the sulfur-rich seed-1 molecule 0.6092781022337287, and the repeated-core seed-2 molecule has an observed score of 0.6107949991985895. The quoted methoxyalkyl/nitrile heteroaryl sulfone is the lowest recorded optimizer example at 0.34184133423484336, whereas ethyne is 0.5. Therefore the sampled differences concern arrangement and connected context, not merely having rings, nitriles or heteroatoms. Both compact and enlarged multi-ring assemblies reach the higher observed region, and bulk alone is not established as the driver. The seed-2 final proposal still belongs to the repeated-core family and scores 0.6079291365669075; neither this nor its trajectory maximum repairs the failed formal task.

per_task.generated_character: The high observed molecules contain halogenated aromatic groups plus free aliphatic ring amines; this generator demonstrably can make such centres. Across the optimizer stream the heavy-atom median is 33, range 1 to 112, with median 4 rings and 2 aromatic rings. The successful seed-0 leader is a 29-heavy-atom biphenyl with a fluorinated benzylic pyrrolidine substituent and an aminoethyl ether ending in another pyrrolidine. The successful seed-1 leader has a chlorophenol tethered to a complex nitrogen-rich polycycle and a pyridyl group. The seed-2 observed leader is a 27-heavy-atom diaryl/benzylic-chloride assembly bearing an aminopiperidine through a propyl linker; this session failed to exit after stop. Conventional arylalkyl amines and ethers are recognizable, but the bridged polycycles and benzylic-halide arrangements need separate route and stereochemical assessment. Parent leaders likewise combined aryl groups and free amines. N-halogen flags are reduced here from Parent 158/870 to 4/870, and from 34/87 to 1/87 in the upper decile; this is descriptive chemical composition, not attribution.
liabilities: The benzylic chloride and unusually fused nitrogen polycycle complicate chemical interpretation; geometry, stability and makeability are unmeasured.
The full stream includes oversized assemblies up to 112 heavy atoms even though none of the upper-decile products reaches 50; this does not justify a universal size filter.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identities are absent from every upper-decile molecule despite all 87 having unassigned graph-perceived centres. The record therefore does not compare the configurations of its fluorinated, chlorinated, benzylic or polycyclic centres.

Free ring amines are present, but coherent protonation alternatives and simpler matched linker/ring-topology variants are not demonstrated by the cited leaders. The neutral graphs do not establish the relevant solution ionisation states.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The successful seed-0 and seed-1 leaders have scores 0.9973551791240318 and 0.9351722724628042. The seed-2 leader has an observed score of 0.9999918725593391 within its failed-stop session. In contrast, the quoted N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine with one dichlorophenyl ring scores 0.0001542080382381353. The sampled upper region retains multiple aryl/polar features and available aliphatic amines rather than only a sulfonamide-bound ring nitrogen. All 87 upper-decile molecules carry halogen, lack the amide/sulfonamide SMARTS flags and have 24 to 34 heavy atoms; the lower decile includes 25 tiny products and 31 products of at least 50 heavy atoms. This is a conditional association across different structures, not evidence of binding, efficacy or a controlled amine-versus-sulfonamide effect.

per_task.generated_character: Products combine aryl rings with fused carbonyl-containing heterocycles and, frequently, piperazine/sulfonamide functionality. The heavy-atom median is 38, range 1 to 77, with median 5 rings and 3 aromatic rings. The best observed seed-0 molecule has 34 heavy atoms, a methylbiphenyl, an arylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine and a fused partially saturated imide/amine bicyclic unit: five rings, two aromatic. The seed-2 high family instead retains an aromatic fused dione, an oxygen-containing ring system and a tethered N-methylpiperazine. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments, but their assembly includes aminal and N-O/peroxide-like junctions in parts of the stream. Typed/generic scaffold coverage is 397/321 versus Parent 283/230, while the upper decile has only 15/11; broader total coverage still concentrates into a small number of upper-score core families.
liabilities: Aminal-like carbon between two nitrogens occurs in 69/87 upper-decile products; this is a connection-chemistry question, not automatic invalidity.

N-O and O-O junctions appear in later products, including the cited final structure, and 24 products shrink to at most six heavy atoms. Neither motif tolerance nor the zero-score fragments establishes a universally useful exclusion rule.
missing_features: Matched scaffold/linker alternatives that retain the combined aryl-carbonyl-polar-ring context are not systematically represented; fragmentation often removes the combination and local variants dominate the upper region.

Specified ring-junction and substituent configuration is missing: 77/87 upper-decile products have unassigned graph-perceived centres, with none assigned. The graphs do not identify any additional hidden target-required functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The quoted seed-0 fused imide/sulfonyl-piperazine molecule scores 0.26788628234534034, and its methylated close relative 0.26496162825115294. NCN and the other highly truncated examples score 0.0. All 87 upper-decile molecules have the sulfonamide SMARTS flag, compared with 9/87 lower-decile molecules; their heavy-atom median is 36 versus lower-decile 20. This observed concentration supports retaining connected aryl, carbonyl and polar-ring context while exploring arrangements. It does not prove that a sulfonamide is required by the objective. Parent upper-decile structures also combine aryl groups, fused diones and nitrogen-containing appendages, with a heavy-atom median of 39. The last seed-2 molecule introduces both an N-O connection and an O-O-containing ring and scores 0.19673227280173666, below that session's earlier 0.21900639466686211 observation.

per_task.generated_character: The stream is dominated by fused dione heterocycles and aryl substituents; upper-scoring products add multiple fluorinated positions and dense ring fusion. Heavy atoms have median 28 and range 1 to 55, with median 4 rings and 4 aromatic rings overall. The seed-1 leader has 30 heavy atoms, six perceived rings and four aromatic rings, with carbon-bound fluorine on aryl, fluoromethyl and saturated-ring positions, a phenol, dione carbonyls and an N-O-containing ring closure. Seed 0 instead reaches an N-fluorinated/N-hydroxy dione with benzyl and fluoropyridyl substituents. The seed-2 leader retains a four-membered diene substituent. These are valence-accepted graphs whose connection and ring chemistry remain questionable. Parent upper-score structures were likewise densely fused fluorinated diones, often with an N-N junction; the Child topology and N-O chemistry differ without isolating an atom replacement effect. All three sessions of this task are successful, even though the seed-2 suite as a whole is failed.
liabilities: The leaders themselves include N-O or N-F chemistry and, in one seed, a four-membered diene ring; these require independent route, geometry and stability assessment.

Across all 870 proposals, N-halogen/O-halogen/single-O-O flags occur in 96/48/12. The low-score repeated-core dimer and tiny fragments show both loss of size balance and failure to preserve useful connected context.
missing_features: Defined configurations of the saturated and fused-ring centres are missing: 85/87 upper-decile molecules have unassigned graph-perceived atom centres and none is assigned.

Coherent alternative core and linker arrangements retaining the empirically favored size and carbon-bound fluorination are sparse among the upper-scoring molecules. The visible records do not show whether less strained or more conventional alternatives would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated seed-1 fused structure scores 0.47433936294182466, the seed-0 N-fluorinated structure 0.3350693772635312, and the four-membered-diene seed-2 structure 0.4132456269332859. The quoted repeated dione/aryl dimer scores 2.79510510122732e-39, and the lower decile includes all 44 products of at most six heavy atoms. Every upper-decile product is halogenated, with heavy-atom median 30 and ring median 6; only five typed and four generic scaffolds cover that upper group. This sampled surface associates intermediate size and specific fluorinated fused arrangements with higher scores, but it cannot separate fluorination, ring fusion, heteroatom placement and seed-family concentration. The seed-2 last N-O-F-containing product scores 0.0022741916338406987: merely adding halogen-containing attachments is not sufficient. None of these scores establishes pharmaceutical activity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-9659e4138ba7, actual code Parent n-d781e302f9f5, L01 Research in Depth epoch 1, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch 10 and 300 accepted trajectory observations per session. These counts include all 4350 observed Child optimizer products, including the two seed-2 sessions that failed after stop; they are chemistry descriptions, not a complete formal evaluation or component attribution. Child N-halogen/O-halogen/single-O-O counts are 156/87/61 versus Parent 371/156/95, while neutral N=O/N-nitroso counts are 243/67 versus 9/8. Thus fewer heteroatom-halogen bonds do not amount to uniformly conventional connection chemistry. The quoted N-nitroso carboxamide is among the highest observed molecules in its session family; other quoted leaders include N-O ring closure or dense sulfur/nitrogen junctions. Definitions and original source/hash mapping are in policy/scratch/r0079-02-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json and policy/scratch/r0079-02-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-measurements.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional attachment chemistry when combining otherwise recognizable aromatic, carbonyl and amine fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make attachment environment and linker identity controllable, preserving distinctions between carbon-bound and heteroatom-bound halogen, free and acylated/sulfonylated amines, and ether versus N-O/O-O junctions. Offer coherent alternatives and let only current-session accepted feedback determine their value. These motifs are structural audit flags, not validated universal filters, synthetic verdicts or demonstrated causes of endpoint loss.

transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves atom configuration unspecified even when its own high-scoring outputs contain stereogenic side chains and fused or substituted rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve chemically coherent stereochemical identities through construction and recombination, including newly formed substituent and ring-junction centres. Compare their value using only clean current-session feedback. Unassigned graph centres do not prove an experimental mixture, and protonation/tautomer treatment is a separate unresolved representation issue rather than an inferred target answer.

These counts include all 4350 observed Child optimizer products, including the two seed-2 sessions that failed after stop; they are chemistry descriptions, not a complete formal evaluation or component attribution. There are 142 Child products with at most 6 heavy atoms and 514 with at least 50, versus Parent 154 and 432. The observed Child maximum is 112 heavy atoms. Let the session determine appropriate molecular scale. Neither a fixed size cutoff nor deletion of every small or large product is warranted by these descriptions, and chemical association is not component attribution.

These counts include all 4350 observed Child optimizer products, including the two seed-2 sessions that failed after stop; they are chemistry descriptions, not a complete formal evaluation or component attribution. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make coherent changes of scaffold topology, linker and polar-group arrangement available alongside local substituent edits, preserving context that has received useful feedback in the current session. Do not turn raw scaffold count into a new optimization target or assume that more diversity, or any specific ring or amine motif, will improve every objective. Whether these alternatives help requires separate evidence.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
